quotes.text: Asking whether MQTT or OPC UA is better is like asking whether TCP or JSON is better. TCP moves information between systems. JSON gives the content a shape that software can read.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear analogy that dissolves the MQTT versus OPC UA debate into transport versus meaning.

quotes.text: A broker delivering a message doesn't prove a business process completed. It proves transport reached the agreed stage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: A broker can distribute data widely without exposing it widely. Those are not the same thing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Installing an MQTT broker does not create a useful namespace and publishing every tag from every PLC does not create a useful namespace either. It creates a large amount of reachable data which is not the same as a shared operating model.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: MQTT and OPC UA solve different problems: MQTT distributes events through a broker, while OPC UA gives machine data structure, types and context at the source.
Governed topic rules, versioned payload contracts with units, source timestamps and quality status, and a stable asset identity matter more than the protocol choice.
Azure IoT Operations provides an edge layer with a local MQTT broker, OPC UA connectors and data flows, but it needs Kubernetes operations, clear ownership and deliberate offline design.
hook: Plants with ERP, MES, Azure and connected machines still argue about whose numbers are right. This episode is for manufacturing, OT and integration architects choosing how MQTT, OPC UA, Azure IoT Operations and Microsoft Fabric fit together. It shows how to separate transport from meaning and design topics, payloads and edge boundaries that survive a second factory.
